opening.headline: Can we determine whether special data, such as medical records, can be included in AI based solely on product conditions?
body: A hospital administrative team wants to automate medical record summaries with AI. The record includes name, diagnosis, prescription, and test results. I know I shouldn't judge it by the same standards as regular business data, but it's not clear what and how it changes.

In this lesson, we will use medical data as an example to identify the plans and contract terms required for special data. We'll look at what a HIPAA readiness plan includes, how it's different in an API, and what role de-identification plays, before ending with commentary on determining whether your medical record summary practice meets the requirements.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain conditions required for special data
You can distinguish between plans and contract conditions required for special data work.

screens.title: Can medical records be stored in AI?
screens.lead: Read the situations below and think about what should be different from your typical work materials.

visual.alt: Illustration highlighting names, diagnoses, prescriptions, and test results in medical history documents.
labels: Product conditions alone are not enough

paragraphs: A hospital administrative team wants to automate medical record summaries with AI. The record contains the patient's name, diagnosis, prescription, and test results. Even if it is the same summary task, it cannot be judged by the same standards as summarizing meeting minutes.

Special data, such as medical or financial, is sensitive and may require legal protection or additional contracts. In this case, the question does not end with whether the product uses data for training. You must also check whether this data can be processed under this plan and contract.
This class uses medical data as an example to see how plan and contract terms are layered on top of product terms.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: If there is a no-retention contract, can I safely include medical data? In class we will see how the two contracts differ.

screens.outro: First, let's think about whether our work has special data.

screens.title: Is there any work that deals with special data?
screens.lead: When you select a question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. The answer will not be submitted, so please think about our work first and then check.

items.prompt: Does our work contain health, financial, identity or biometric information?
items.answer: Even if you don't think you're dealing with it directly, it's often mixed in with customer service records or personnel documents. You need to re-check the source of the data.

items.prompt: Is it already allowed to put that data into AI?
items.answer: Allowance depends not only on the type of material, but also on the product and plan you include it in. Since there are cases where the fact that it has been permitted is reported without any basis, it is important to be able to verify the basis.

items.prompt: If allowed, under what contract or plan is it allowed?
items.answer: If you can't answer this question right away, you may be writing without checking the terms of the contract. In this lesson, we outline the criteria for inspection. Inspection is not difficult and can start with three questions.

screens.outro: Now let’s start with what a HIPAA preparedness plan includes.

screens.title: What a HIPAA Readiness Plan Requires
screens.lead: When you select an item, the text expands. Take a look at what Claude Enterprise's HIPAA-ready configuration includes and doesn't include, step by step.

items.title: What is included
items.body: Claude Enterprise has HIPAA-ready configurations for organizations that process protected health information (PHI). Includes features and safeguards designed to support Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and HIPAA compliance requirements. The target audience is medical institutions, health insurance, medical data processors and their business associates.

items.title: By what criteria do you determine whether it is necessary?
items.body: The standards presented in the document are simple. Will you be handling PHI with Claude? If so, you need a HIPAA-ready product with a BAA. This question cannot be replaced by the good preservation conditions of a product.

items.title: Are all features included?
items.body: Not included. Turning on HIPAA does not bring all features under BAA, and features fall into three categories: BAA-enforced, enabled but not BAA-enforced, and disabled. PHI must be processed only in functions covered by the BAA. Which features belong where are written in the implementation guide, which is the reference document.

items.title: What Happens to Claude Code and Cowork?
items.body: Simply turning on HIPAA does not bring Claude Code and Cowork into BAA. Primary Owner must apply separate HIPAA configuration. Before application, Cowork is available but not applied, and Claude Code is applied only when no preservation is turned on. After application, cloud features will be disabled.

items.title: Who turns it on and how
items.body: Only the Primary Owner of an Enterprise plan organization can accept a BAA and turn on HIPAA. Team plan and personal plan (Free, Pro, Max) cannot be turned on. Turning it on will return some settings to their defaults, and once you turn them on, you can't go back to them in your organization settings. Therefore, you should review the BAA and Implementation Guide before turning it on. The Primary Owner is the only one who can change the settings, so please designate a contact person in advance.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen the structure of the plan, let's compare how they differ in the API.

screens.title: HIPAA readiness and no-retention requirements for APIs
screens.lead: Click the toggle to cycle through how no-retention and HIPAA-ready are different arrangements.

states.label: No preservation
states.body: No-preservation is an agreement to not store prompts and responses after they are returned. Although it reduces retention concerns, it does not replace a BAA required for processing PHI. Entering PHI with only no preservation and no BAA does not meet the requirements. In other words, the fact that retention conditions are good is a separate issue from eligibility for processing PHI. Additionally, even if there is no retention, there remain exceptions to storage due to safety markings or legal requirements.

states.label: HIPAA Preparation
states.body: HIPAA readiness is a separate commitment that applies BAA as well as broader privacy and security safeguards such as encryption, access controls, and audit logs. The focus is on protecting PHI throughout its lifecycle rather than requiring immediate deletion. According to the document, organizations that handle PHI are HIPAA-ready and do not need to have a non-preservation agreement in place. If a HIPAA organization sends a feature that is not in the eligibility table, the API will block with a 400 error, and consumer plans, consoles, and partner platforms are outside this scope. OpenAI also only allows processing of PHI for customers with a BAA and Healthcare Addendum, and writes that live web searches are not HIPAA eligible.

screens.outro: There are times when a contract alone may not be enough. Let’s look at the role of de-identification.

screens.title: Why use de-identification and additional contracts together?
screens.lead: Read the text below and select the highlighted passages. An explanation of how de-identification is used with contracts appears.

data.text: De-identification of personal identifiers, such as names, contact details, and identification numbers, means removing or replacing them before input. It reduces exposure risk, but contractual requirements still apply. Even with a BAA, only BAA-covered features may be used, so de-identification provides an additional safeguard. Google Cloud documentation explains that, to achieve zero data retention, customers must take action for each logging area. Check contractual terms and settings together.

marks.span: removing or replacing them before input
marks.note: If you don't need names or identification numbers in your summary, the simplest way is to leave them out before entering them. This reduces personally identifiable information reaching the provider.

This is because de-identification may be incomplete and the conditions required for documentation are tied to the type of data. De-identification should not lead to skipping contract checks. The two methods are an overlay relationship, not a replacement relationship.

marks.span: only BAA-covered features may be used
marks.note: Even if you have a BAA, PHI cannot be processed if the function you use is outside the scope of coverage. De-identification reduces the risk in this case once more.

marks.span: customers must take action for each logging area
marks.note: In Google Cloud, prompt logging, advanced model logging, and search grounding logs should be inspected by area. If you only check the contract and miss the settings, zero retention will not be achieved.

screens.outro: Now, let's explain the conditions of the medical record summary task.

screens.title: Commentary: Requirements for medical record summary work
screens.lead: Let's break down the conditions that the hospital administrative team must meet to summarize medical records in five steps. Select the next arrow to proceed.

steps.title: Condition 1: Plan
steps.body: We exclude Personal and Team plans because they cannot turn on HIPAA. Use an Enterprise HIPAA Readiness Plan with a BAA or an API organization with HIPAA enabled. At this stage, paths that paste medical records into the consumer account will be removed from the whitelist.  It is safe to specify the name of the allowed path.

steps.title: Condition 2: Functional
steps.body: Turn on only features covered by BAA. Turn off features that are not subject to BAA, such as live web browsing. If a HIPAA organization sends a non-eligible feature to the API, it will be blocked with an error, but no error does not mean it is in BAA scope, so we manually match the list of features. The results of the match are tabulated with the feature name and classification.

steps.title: Condition 3: Conservation
steps.body: Where possible, use no retention together and note any exception periods for legal retention and safe storage. HIPAA-ready and no-retention are different commitments, so check for each. Don't assume that one is in place because the other is in place.

steps.title: Condition 4: De-identification
steps.body: If the summary does not require patient names and identification numbers, remove them before entering them. De-identification is not a substitute for contracting, but rather an additional safeguard that reduces the risk of exposure.

steps.title: Condition 5: Administrator settings
steps.body: Tools like Claude Code and Cowork do not write to PHI until the Primary Owner applies a separate configuration. Applying the configuration will disable cloud functionality, so make sure your business does not rely on that functionality. If your business relies on cloud sessions, you may be judged to not be able to use them to handle PHI.

screens.outro: Now that we have gathered the conditions, we will summarize how to determine whether they are met.

screens.title: Explanation: Determination of whether conditions are met
screens.lead: When you select an item, confirmation methods and judgment criteria will appear. Look in the order of plan, features, and retention.

items.answer: Check your contract to see if you have a BAA in place, and check your organization settings to see if HIPAA is active. There must be a checkmark in the HIPAA Compliance item on the settings screen to indicate it is activated. Even if there is a contract, if it is not activated on the screen, the processing conditions have not yet been met. If not indicated, the organization is not active.

Verify that the features you use are in the BAA coverage list against the eligibility table in the document. Features that are not listed or classified as available but not applicable are not used with PHI. The same contrast is repeated even when features are added or renamed.

Check whether No Retention is enabled and what are the reasons for exceptions to Safe and Legal Storage. If there is no no-retention, we separately determine whether the default retention period meets business standards. For example, ensure that the default 30-day deletion does not conflict with the hospital's record retention standards.

items.prompt: What do I do if even one thing is not confirmed?
items.answer: We make the work conditional and do not include PHI until verification is complete. Unconfirmed items are recorded by setting a deadline for confirmation with the person in charge. Operating unchecked is the highest risk. Unconfirmed items must be reopened within the specified deadline and the results must be recorded.

screens.outro: Now that I've finished judging, I'll summarize the main points.

screens.title: Key Takeaway: Special data requires a plan and contract
screens.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.

paragraphs: Special data looks at the plan and contract together, not the product terms. A HIPAA preparedness plan consists of a BAA and a scope of covered functions, with PHI only being processed by functions covered by the BAA. No-retention and HIPAA readiness are different commitments, and de-identification is an additional safeguard.

Judgments are made in the following order: plan, function, and preservation. If even one is not confirmed, it is set as conditional and no PHI is included. Please record the verified evidence along with the document name. Having these records can help us explain in the event of an audit or internal review on what basis we permitted processing of your PHI. You should also recheck in the same order every time you introduce a new feature or change your organization settings.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: No preservation does not eliminate the need for BAA.

checks.intro: Check the relationship between the two agreements yourself. This confirmation is not logged.
checks.q: What is appropriate in relation to non-retention and HIPAA preparation?
options: It is a separate agreement, and HIPAA preparation applies broader privacy and security safeguards.
If there is no preservation, BAA is not necessary
When you turn on HIPAA, all features are included in BAA
These are two names for the same contract.
checks.explain: No-retention is a no-storage agreement, and HIPAA readiness is a separate agreement that includes a BAA.

wrong.1: Processing of PHI requires a BAA and is not a substitute for no retention.
wrong.2: Functions are divided into BAA applied, available but not applied, and disabled.
wrong.3: The two agreements have different purposes and scopes and are not intended to replace each other.

checks.correctFeedback: That's right. The two agreements have different purposes and are not substitutes for each other.
checks.incorrectFeedback: There is a view that sees the two agreements as the same. Think back to what each contract covers.

checks.intro: Think about the sequence for determining whether the conditions for a medical record summary task are met. Arrange the items in the appropriate order.
checks.q: Summary of medical records Arrange them in the appropriate order to determine whether the conditions for the task are met.
items: Plan: Enter into BAA and confirm HIPAA active status
Function: Compare eligibility table with BAA list.
Retention: Activate no retention and check exception reasons
If there are unconfirmed items, leave them conditional and withhold PHI input.
checks.explain: Check plan, function, and retention in order, and if any of them are unconfirmed, PHI will not be entered until confirmed.
checks.correctFeedback: The order is correct. It even includes the principle of not including PHI until verification is complete.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The order is out of order. Consider a flow that starts with the contract terms on which the decision is based.

glossary.def: This is sensitive data that requires legal protection or additional contracts, such as health or finance.
A plan or setup from a provider that supports the processing of PHI with a BAA and safeguards in place.
This is a business partnership agreement concluded in a business partnership dealing with health information. It serves as a standard for the scope of applicable functions.
Processing that reduces the risk of exposure by removing or replacing personally identifiable items.

misconceptions.myth: Medical data is also safe if it is not preserved.
misconceptions.fact: No-retention and HIPAA preparation are separate, and processing of PHI requires a separate BAA.

misconceptions.myth: All features are included when you turn on the HIPAA plan.
misconceptions.fact: Whether or not BAA is applied varies depending on the feature. They are divided into three categories: applied, available but not applied, and inactive.

misconceptions.myth: If de-identified, there is no need for a contract.
misconceptions.fact: De-identification is an additional safeguard and does not replace required engagement.

closing.lead: We recapitulate the key points of this lesson.
points: Special data looks at plans and contracts together.
We process PHI only in functions covered by the BAA.
No-retention and HIPAA readiness are different commitments.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for your own reflection only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: Under what plans and contracts are the special data we handle processed, and what functions are not included in that scope?
